items.label: Theorem 1
items.statementLatex:
\label{thm:main}
For every $0<c_1<2/3$ and $2/3\le c_2<1$, the parameters in this
section can be chosen so that $f$ in \eqref{eq:objective} belongs to
$C^2(\R^2)$, has a globally H\"older continuous Hessian with exponent
$1/2$, and satisfies $\frac12I\preceq\nabla^2f(x)\preceq\frac32I$
for all $x\in\R^2$. With the positive definite initial matrix in
\eqref{eq:counterexample-initial-data} and positive step lengths in
\eqref{eq:counterexample-recurrence}, classical DFP is well defined and
every step satisfies \eqref{eq:armijo} and \eqref{eq:strong-curvature},
but $\|\nabla f(x_k)\|\longrightarrow G_\infty>0$.
The same conclusion holds in every dimension $n\ge2$.

items.label: Corollary 2
items.statementLatex:
\label{cor:identity-initialization}
Fix any pair $(c_1,c_2)$ in the range of Theorem~\ref{thm:main}.  There exist
$\widetilde f\in C^2(\R^2)$ with a globally H\"older continuous Hessian of
exponent $1/2$, an initial point $\widetilde x_0\in\R^2$, a sequence of positive
step lengths $\{\alpha_k\}_{k\ge0}$, and constants
$0<\widetilde m\le \widetilde M<\infty$ with
$\widetilde m I\preceq\nabla^2\widetilde f(x)\preceq\widetilde M I$
for all $x\in\R^2$. For this objective function, classical DFP initialized with $\widetilde H_0=I$ is well
defined, and every accepted step satisfies \eqref{eq:armijo} and
\eqref{eq:strong-curvature}.  Nevertheless,
$\liminf_{k\to\infty}\|\nabla\widetilde f(\widetilde x_k)\|>0$.
The same conclusion holds in every dimension $n\ge2$.

items.label: Theorem 3
items.statementLatex:
\label{thm:planar-convergence}
Let $f\in C^2(\R^2)$ satisfy $\nabla^2f(x)\succeq\mu I$ for all
$x\in\R^2$ and some $\mu>0$. Let $x_0\in\R^2$ and $H_0\succ0$
be arbitrary, and fix $0<c_1<c_2<1$. Suppose $\nabla^2f$ is locally
Lipschitz continuous on a neighborhood of the initial level set
$K=\{x\in\R^2:f(x)\le f(x_0)\}$.
Then classical DFP with update \eqref{eq:dfp-update} and positive step
lengths satisfying \eqref{eq:armijo} and \eqref{eq:weak-curvature}
either reaches the unique minimizer $x_*$ in finitely many iterations or
generates an infinite sequence satisfying
$x_k\longrightarrow x_*$ and $\|\nabla f(x_k)\|\longrightarrow0$.

items.label: Lemma 6
items.statementLatex:
\label{lem:center-manifold}
After cancellation of the explicit singular factors, $\mathcal F$ has a real
analytic extension near $(0,2,1)$.  Its derivative there has one eigenvalue
equal to $1$ and two other eigenvalues
$-1/9$ and $0$, so it has a
locally invariant one-dimensional $C^7$ center manifold
$p=p(\epsilon)$ and $h=h(\epsilon)$,
on which
\begin{align}
p(\epsilon)&=2+\frac{198}{5}\epsilon^3
-\frac95\epsilon^4+O(\epsilon^5),
&h(\epsilon)&=1+8\epsilon^3+O(\epsilon^5),
\label{eq:center-curve}\\
\epsilon_+&=\epsilon-\frac32\epsilon^4
+\frac54\epsilon^5+O(\epsilon^6).
\label{eq:epsilon-map}
\end{align}

items.label: Lemma 11
items.statementLatex:
\label{lem:planar-degeneration}
Let $f\in C^2(\R^2)$ be $\mu$-strongly convex, where $\mu>0$.
Consider an infinite sequence of nonstationary iterates with
$g_k=\nabla f(x_k)$, $s_k=-\alpha_kH_kg_k$,
$x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k$, and $y_k=g_{k+1}-g_k$, where $H_k\succ0$,
$\alpha_k>0$, and every step satisfies \eqref{eq:armijo} and
\eqref{eq:weak-curvature} for fixed $0<c_1<c_2<1$.
Suppose $H_ky_{k-1}=s_{k-1}$ for $k\ge1$. Put
\begin{equation}\label{eq:planar-scalar-definition}
\ell_k=\|s_k\|,\qquad
\kappa_k=\frac{s_k^Ty_k}{\ell_k^2},\qquad
\lambda_k=\kappa_{k-1}\det H_k\quad(k\ge1).
\end{equation}
If $x_k$ does not converge to the unique minimizer $x_*$, then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:planar-degeneration}
0<\lambda_k\le C\ell_{k-1}\ell_k\longrightarrow0
\end{equation}
for all sufficiently large $k$, with $C$ independent of $k$.
Moreover, $\{H_k\}$ is bounded and $\lambda_{\min}(H_k)\to0$.
